statement: The value $V$, in dollars, of an office printer $t$ years after it was bought is modeled by $V(t) = 1{,}260 - 90t$. According to the model, after how many full years will the printer first be worth less than one-fourth of its purchase price?

choices.misconception: I found when the printer is worth nothing, $1260 / 90 = 14$, instead of when it drops below one-fourth of its price.
I solved $1260 - 90t = 315$ to get 10.5 and rounded down to 10, but after 10 years the printer is still worth 360 dollars.
I found when the printer had lost one-fourth of its value, $90t > 315$, which gave $t > 3.5$, so I said 4 years.

hints: The purchase price is the value when $t = 0$.
Find one-fourth of the purchase price, then solve $1260 - 90t < 315$ for $t$ and think about whole years.

solutions.reliable: The purchase price is $V(0) = 1260$ dollars, and one-fourth of it is $315$. Solve $1260 - 90t < 315$: $-90t < -945$, so $t > 10.5$. The first full year with $t > 10.5$ is $t = 11$. Check: $V(10) = 360$, still above $315$, while $V(11) = 270$, below it. Key idea: the slope is the yearly loss, and 'first time below' means rounding the boundary up to the next whole year.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
